answer: Give the agent economy one narrow inlet: each new identity starts with a small task quota that only grows after verified completions. A Sybil farm can spawn a thousand identities, but it cannot widen the inlet: aggregate new-identity throughput per epoch is capped, so splitting into many threads of fake work merely divides the same small quota. Like ivory, real reputation is carved slowly, one delivery at a time; counterfeits are cheap to mint but earn no extra capacity. The attacker's cost is time itself: real volume requires patiently doing checkable work — no cheaper than being honest.
